# Psalm 55 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For-the-choirmaster. With-stringed-instruments. A-Maskil of-David.

**2** Give-ear to-my-prayer, O-God, and-do-not hide-Yourself from-my-plea.

**3** Attend to-me and-answer-me; I-am-restless in-my-complaint and-I-moan,

**4** because-of the-voice of-the-enemy, because-of the-oppression of-the-wicked; for they-cast iniquity upon-me, and-in-anger they-bear-a-grudge against-me.

**5** My-heart writhes within-me, and-the-terrors of-death have-fallen upon-me.

**6** Fear and-trembling come upon-me, and-horror overwhelms-me.

**7** And-I-say, 'Who will-give-me wings like-a-dove? I-would-fly-away and-be-at-rest.

**8** Behold, I-would-wander far-away; I-would-lodge in-the-wilderness. Selah.

**9** I-would-hasten my-escape from-the-rushing wind [and] tempest.'

**10** Confuse, Lord, divide their-tongue, for I-see violence and-strife in-the-city.

**11** Day and-night they-go-around on-her-walls, and-iniquity and-trouble [are] in-her-midst.

**12** Destruction [is] in-her-midst; oppression and-deceit do-not depart from-her-square.

**13** For [it is] not an-enemy [who] taunts-me — then-I-could-bear [it]; not [one who] hates-me [who] magnifies [himself] against-me — then-I-could-hide from-him.

**14** But-you — a-man my-equal, my-companion, my-close-friend.

**15** Together we-made-sweet our-counsel; in-the-house of-God we-walked with-the-throng.

**16** Let-death come-upon-them; let-them-go-down to-Sheol alive, for evil [is] in-their-dwelling, in-their-midst.

**17** As-for-me, to-God I-call, and-YHWH saves-me.

**18** Evening and-morning and-noon I-complain and-moan, and-He-hears my-voice.

**19** He-redeems in-peace my-soul from-the-battle against-me, for in-multitudes they-are with-me.

**20** God hears and-humbles-them — the-One-sitting [enthroned] from-of-old — Selah — because there-are-no changes for-them, and-they-do-not fear God.

**21** He-stretched-out his-hand against his-allies; he-profaned his-covenant.

**22** Smooth [were] the-butter-words of-his-mouth, but-war [was in] his-heart; his-words were-softer than-oil, but-they [were] drawn swords.

**23** Cast upon YHWH your-burden, and-He sustains-you; He never allows the-righteous to-be-shaken.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **55:7**: 'Wings like a dove' — the desire to flee suffering entirely. The psalmist fantasizes about escape before choosing to trust.

— EMET
